claims.text: The initial FeCoNi material is single-phase FCC.
Single-phase FCC FeCoNi or its high-entropy-alloy derivatives have high saturation magnetization.
The coercive fields of the stated single-phase FCC materials are typically no greater than 100 Oe.
Laser powder bed fusion with rapid cooling can induce a controlled multiphase microstructure in FeCoNi.
Rapidly cooled additive manufacturing can form nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates in FeCoNi.
Rapidly cooled additive manufacturing can refine the grain structure of FeCoNi.
The proposed nanoscale precipitates can be generated without changing the overall FeCoNi composition.
Nanoscale precipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Refined grain boundaries act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Obstruction of domain-wall motion by the induced microstructural heterogeneities increases coercivity relative to homogeneous single-phase material.
The intervention will increase the room-temperature coercive field beyond 100 Oe relative to conventionally produced single-phase FCC FeCoNi.
The intervention will maintain high saturation magnetization while increasing coercivity.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends sensitively on additive-manufacturing energy density and cooling rate.
